Check if the recipient is not the designated beneficiary

boxes.notes: Printed on Copy A only; a recipient's copy never carries it. Declared because the face prints it (FR-016).

boxes.label: If the fair market value (FMV) is shown below, see Pub. 970, Tax Benefits for Education, for how to figure earnings.

codes.label: Excess contributions plus earnings taxable in the calendar year
Excess contributions plus earnings taxable in the prior calendar year

document.notes: Box 1 = box 2 + box 3; the EARNINGS in box 2 are the only potentially taxable figure. Routing box 1 to income would report the return of basis as income - see aggregate 1099q.2. Checkbox 4b 'QTP to Roth IRA' is new on the Rev. April 2025 revision (SECURE 2.0 section 126 rollovers). Whether any of box 2 is taxable is not on the document; it depends on the beneficiary's qualified education expenses, which is why the route carries a question.

face_not_boxes.because: '4 Type of transfer:' is the caption over two checkboxes, declared 4a and 4b.
'5 Distribution is from:' is the caption over three checkboxes, declared 5a, 5b and 5c.

extraction.note: The note that stood here — "Azure ships no prebuilt-tax model for this form" — was STALE, and re-verified as stale twice (2026-09-24 and 2026-09-29) against Azure-Samples `schema/2024-11-30-ga/us-tax/`. v4.0 (2024-11-30 GA) publishes this model. Boxes 1-3 answer as `Box<n>`; boxes 4 and 5 are CHECKBOXES that Azure answers as a selection, so `fields` says which declared box each selected value is. Box 4b (QTP to Roth IRA) has no Azure field of its own — the model answers box 4 as one boolean — so a 4b transfer is not read by this model and is not silently filed as 4a.
